_note: THE FILE-INPUT ROUTING LAW (d-ios#1023/#1025/#1026, d-android#281/#285, ported). Neither WKOpenPanelParameters nor Android's FileChooserParams reliably exposes the input's `accept`, so the page reports it through a shim and NATIVE ROUTES ON THAT HINT ALONE. The decision is subtle in three places that this corpus exists to pin. (1) THE CAMERA'S MEDIA-TYPE ARRAY, not its capture mode, is what draws the PHOTO/VIDEO toggle — `accept="image/*"` with `capture` used to open a toggling camera and could hand a stills-only page back a .mov, even though the mode was correctly pinned to photo. So a camera route carries a SCOPE. (2) A MIXED image+video accept has no narrowing to apply, so it belongs on the source sheet (which offers camera AND library) rather than an un-narrowed library — narrowing to 'both' is not narrowing. (3) A NON-MEDIA accept (.pdf, application/*, or a media+document mix) belongs in a DOCUMENT PICKER, the only picker that can actually enforce those types; an image picker cannot show a PDF at all. An ABSENT accept means the page asked for anything, which is the sheet. `capture` wins whenever present and meaningful, and the scope still narrows what that camera may return. `nativeInterception:false` is the `filepicker://…?native_overwrite=false` switch: WKUIDelegate cannot hand a claimed panel back to WebKit, so 'off' means the sheet — the same sources WebKit's own sheet offers — never 'let WebKit do it'. Cases are {accept, capture, nativeInterception?} -> route. Runners: TS (packages/kernel/src/upload.ts), Kotlin (:core UploadRoutingConformanceTest), Swift (DSXFileUploadPolicy.route, record lane).
